That's interesting... it should be there, even if you don't have any proprietary devices, as I recall.

You don't even need to reinstall; you can troubleshoot this from the LiveCD/UBS installer. Once it's booted up, open a terminal and check to see if you have any configured interfaces:

ifconfig

You'll see one for the loopback, but ignore that. Hopefully you'll have one for the wired connection labeled lan0 or eth0 or something like that. If the cable is plugged in, it should have automagically acquired an IP, and the output should contain that, too.

More than likely, though, since you said this hasn't been working, you'll only see the loopback interface. There's a couple of things you can check that are a little unorthodox to see if the system is even trying to bring the network up:

dmesg | grep -i ethernet

That will print out the boot messages and let you know whether the system even saw the card, and hopefully that it did load a driver for it, but it should also pickup if it failed to find one. 

sudo tail -f /var/log/messages

This will give a continuous, realtime readout of the syslog. What it's good for in your situation is so you can plug and unplug your ethernet cable and see if it's generating any log data; something like "status: up," and "status: down."

EDIT: On that tail command, the Googles suggest that Mint may be storing the syslog in /var/log/syslog now instead of /var/log/messages, so you may have to change the target accordingly. I don't have a running instance handy to confirm.
